ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Loi modifiée du 12 novembre 2004 relative à la lutte contre le blanchiment et contre le financement du terrorisme (AML/CFT Law of 12 November 2004, as amended by the Law of 10 August 2018 and the Law of 25 December 2020); Loi du 13 janvier 2019 portant institution d'un registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (Beneficial Owner Register Law, as amended); Règlement grand-ducal du 1er février 2019 portant exécution de la loi du 13 janvier 2019; CSSF Regulation N° 12-02 and CSSF Circulars 18/698 and 20/735; Loi modifiée du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales (Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies, as amended by the Law of 23 July 2016 introducing the Société en commandite spéciale); Loi du 21 décembre 2012 relative à l'accès à la profession de commissionnaire en douane; Regulation (EU) No 952/2013 (Union Customs Code).
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access — the Luxembourg RBE (Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs) is not a fully public register; access is restricted to competent authorities (CRF/FIU, CSSF, tax, customs and judicial authorities), to AML/CFT obliged entities in the course of their client due diligence, and to any person or entity demonstrating a legitimate interest, consistent with the Law of 13 January 2019 (as amended) and the CJEU judgments of 22 November 2022 (C-37/20 and C-601/20).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille Convention of 5 October 1961 (apostille issued by the designated authority of the originating state)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney in favour of the Luxembourg General Partner and/or appointed authorized signatories
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary or other competent issuing authority in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille where the country of origin is a contracting state; otherwise full consular legalization through the Luxembourg Embassy or Consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport and proof of residential address of every natural-person UBO and manager
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary, lawyer or other authorized certifying officer in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization depending on the contracting-state status of the country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Extract of criminal record (casier judiciaire / police clearance certificate) for each manager, General Partner and UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent judicial or police authority of the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization; certified French or German translation by a sworn Luxembourg translator

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-wealth / source-of-funds declaration for each UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Correspondent or relationship bank of the UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized signature chain; apostille only where expressly required by the receiving Luxembourg AML/CFT professional

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Domiciliation agreement (contrat de domiciliation) with an approved Luxembourg domiciliation agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg domiciliation agent authorized under the Law of 31 May 1999 (PSF, attorney, notary, chartered accountant or bailiff)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: No apostille required — Luxembourg private deed signed in original form

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory PEP status determination and enhanced due diligence under Article 3(2) of the AML/CFT Law of 12 November 2004, applying the FATF 40 Recommendations; systematic screening of all UBOs, managers, General Partners and counterparties against (i) the UN Security Council consolidated sanctions lists, (ii) the EU consolidated financial sanctions list, (iii) the US OFAC SDN list and 50% ownership-derivation rules where USD transactions are planned, (iv) the UK HMT consolidated list, and (v) any domestic Luxembourg restrictive measures; adverse-media screening on commercial databases (e.g., World-Check, Dow Jones, LexisNexis); fuzzy-logic name-matching with immediate alert clearance procedures; retention of screening evidence for at least five years after termination of the business relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS); online filing via the LBR e-filing portal at www.lbr.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Registration and filing content is accepted in French, German or Luxembourgish; French is the operative registry language. The corporate name must be expressed in Latin-script characters; non-Latin-script names require a statutory transliteration with a certified translation. The SCSp name must be preceded or followed by the compulsory suffix 'SCSp' or 'Société en commandite spéciale'. Names must be distinctive, not misleading, not contrary to public policy and public order, and must not create confusion with an existing RCS-registered name or a protected trademark.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banque / Bank (statutorily restricted to credit institutions licensed by the CSSF)
Assurance / Insurance (restricted to licensed insurance undertakings under the Law of 7 December 2015)
Fiduciaire / Trust Company (requires professional authorization and may mislead as to regulated fiduciary activity)
Société Nationale / État / Luxembourg (implies state affiliation and requires ministerial authorization)
Université / Croix-Rouge / Charitable (protected names requiring prior consent)
Commissionnaire en Douane / Customs Broker (misleading absent the license required under the Law of 21 December 2012)
Fonds / Fund / SIF / SICAV (requires CSSF authorization for the regulated activity)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon a name rejection decision by the RCS registrar, the applicant must first file a written request for reconsideration with the Registrar within 15 days of notification. If the registrar confirms the refusal, the applicant may initiate judicial proceedings before the commercial chamber of the Luxembourg District Court (Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg, chambre commerciale) by way of a petition or assignation against the State (Ministry of Justice) within one month of the confirmation decision; representation by a Luxembourg-licensed avocat is mandatory. In parallel, the applicant may file a fresh name reservation using a different distinctive element, preserving the 30-day validity window of any alternative reservation.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A purely virtual or domiciliation-only registered office is legally permissible for an SCSp under the Law of 31 May 1999 on the domiciliation of companies, provided the domiciliation agent is an approved professional (PSF, attorney, notary, chartered accountant or bailiff) and the SCSp does not conduct actual business at that address. However, for a licensed customs brokerage house, the customs authorities (Administration des douanes et accises) require a genuine operational establishment and business premises for the exercise of the customs broker activity; therefore a full-service physical office or a serviced office with actual staff presence is commercially mandatory to obtain and maintain the customs broker license.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High — estimated 55-65% likelihood of an unannounced on-site inspection within the first 36 months of operations, driven by the mandatory licensing and fit-and-proper supervision regime for customs brokers (Law of 21 December 2012), the customs audit programmes of the Administration des douanes et accises under Article 48 of the Union Customs Code, and the AML/CFT on-site supervision powers of the CRF/FIU over obliged non-financial professionals.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended, Articles 125-1 through 125-10 (société en commandite spéciale); Law of 23 July 2016; Civil Code Articles 1832-1844 as suppletive partnership law
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Deed of Partnership (Acte de Société) and accompanying RCS registration form; may be executed as a private writing or a notarial deed
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No legal minimum capital for an SCSp; partners agree on contributions and payment schedules in the partnership deed; no escrow or capital blocking account is mandated under Luxembourg law
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: Pro-Forma First Board Resolution of the General Partner of [SCSp]. Upon due convocation, the board of the general partner unanimously resolves: (i) to approve the subscription to the partnership interests as set out in the initial contribution schedule; (ii) to adopt the registered office at [address], Luxembourg; (iii) to appoint [Name] as manager/gérant with full authority to represent the partnership; (iv) to authorize the filing of the partnership deed with the Luxembourg Business Registers and completion of all statutory formalities; and (v) to engage licensed customs brokers as required, with expenses borne by the partnership. This resolution is effective immediately and may be executed in counterparts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Online Name Reservation Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File a name reservation request through the LBR e-application portal, stating the proposed corporate name of the SCSp and the general partner’s details. The name must not already be registered and must comply with Luxembourg public order and language requirements. Upon approval, the reserved name is valid for a limited period.
required_dossiers: Copy of the general partner’s certificate of existence or resolution
Passport or ID copies of the intended manager
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name request is rejected, submit a written objection within 15 days; propose an alternative name or appeal the refusal before the administrative courts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of the Partnership Deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Civil-Law Notary (Notaire) or Private Signature of Partners
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the partnership deed (contrat de société) containing the legal form (SCSp), corporate name, registered office, corporate object (customs brokerage and transit management), duration, capital contributions, and management provisions. Execute the deed in French or German, either before a Luxembourg notary or by private signing with all partners, and initial all pages.
required_dossiers: Capital contribution schedule and proof of cash or in-kind valuation
Identity documents and address proof of each partner and manager
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies inconsistencies, revise the draft and obtain new signatures; private deeds may be re-executed by the partners.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing with the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – RCS Registration Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After execution, file the deed with the RCS via the notary or directly through the LBR online portal. Attach the required dossiers and pay the filing fee. The RCS assigns a registration number and issues an official registration certificate.
required_dossiers: Executed partnership deed (original or certified notarial copy)
RCS registration form (Form C or Form D)
Statutory declaration by the manager(s) confirming no criminal convictions or bankruptcy
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a query, cure the deficiency within one month by filing corrected documents; otherwise pay a partial reevaluation fee and resubmit the relevant form.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in the Electronic Compendium of Companies (RES)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Official Publications Department
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The RCS automatically transmits the registration extract for publication in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RES). Verify the published extract and retain it as conclusive evidence of the SCSp’s existence for third parties.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RES publication is delayed or incorrect, notify the RCS in writing and provide a corrected extract to be re-published at no additional charge if the error is attributable to the registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Administrative Registration (VAT, EORI and Social Security)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l’Enregistrement, des Domaines et de la TVA; Administration des Douanes et Accises; Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a Luxembourg VAT number through the direct e-space of the registration administration; obtain an Economic Operators Registration and Identification (EORI) number from the Customs and Excise Administration for customs clearance operations; register the first employee or manager with the social security centre if applicable.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the VAT or EORI application is queried, provide a supplementary declaration with the missing information; administrative remedies under the tax and customs procedure codes apply.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Administration des Douanes et Accises (Luxembourg Customs and Excise Administration), Ministry of Finance
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Customs Brokerage Licence (Licence de commissionnaire en douane) issued under the Union Customs Code and national implementing rules

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Class B – Registration (environmental permit mandatory for a customs brokerage house operating bonded storage facilities; no full EIA for administrative offices unless the project exceeds the thresholds under the Law of 15 May 2008)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharges must meet the limits set by the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 20 October 1994 and EU directives; VOC concentration thresholds under the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 5 March 2004; waste handling records per Law of 21 March 2012 on waste management.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety clearance from the Corps Grand-Ducal d'Incendie et de Secours (CGDIS); structural load inspection certificate by a licensed engineer; municipal zoning/building permit; occupational health and safety registration with the Service de Santé au Travail (external prevention service).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Luxembourg operates a functionally split national tax administration: (1) Administration des contributions directes (ACD, Luxembourg Inland Revenue) - competent for corporate income tax (impôt sur le revenu des collectivités), municipal business tax (impôt commercial communal), net wealth tax (impôt sur la fortune) and all direct tax registration, with e-filing channelled through the national portal MyGuichet.lu and the ACD digital filing systems. (2) Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) - competent for the TVA (VAT), registration duties and stamp duties, operating the VAT registration and electronic VAT return portal. (3) Administration des douanes et accises (ADA) - Luxembourg Customs and Excise - competent for customs law, export/import clearance, AEO decisions and the licensing of customs brokers under the Union Customs Code.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Luxembourg-established SCSp the procedure is centralized: (1) Formation and RCS registration - execute the notarized partnership agreement and publish it in the electronic register of the Luxembourg Business Registers (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés); the RCS assigns the matricule (national business registration number), which functions as the entity's statutory identifier for all Luxembourg tax files. (2) Direct tax file - upon RCS publication, the ACD automatically opens the direct tax dossier for the SCSp; the transparent partnership does not itself bear corporate income tax, but ACD practice requires an informative filing so that resident partners may integrate their allocable shares in their own tax returns. (3) VAT registration - the SCSp applies to the AEDT for a Luxembourg VAT identification number (format LU + 8 digits) using the standard registration application accompanied by the RCS excerpt, a summary of the partnership agreement and proof of the customs-broker licence; registration is effective from the date of first taxable supply. (4) Foreign taxable persons without an RCS seat - a non-resident supplier making Luxembourg-taxable supplies not subject to the reverse charge must register directly with the AEDT; if the only Luxembourg supplies are reverse-charged B2B services, registration is generally not required, although the customer must be notified of the reverse charge. (5) Customs licence - the brokerage house must hold an ADA-issued customs broker authorization before acting as an indirect customs representative; the ADA application must evidence professional reliability, solvency, customs-law knowledge and an EORI registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible - statutory tax transparency without election: the SCSp is a contractual special limited partnership without legal personality. For direct taxes (corporate income tax, municipal business tax and net wealth tax), the SCSp itself is not the taxpayer; each partner (associé commandité and associé commanditaire) is treated as deriving its allocable share of the SCSp's income, gains, deductions and net wealth directly. Resident partners are taxed in Luxembourg on their allocable shares; non-resident partners are taxable in Luxembourg only to the extent the SCSp derives Luxembourg-source income (e.g., Luxembourg real estate or a Luxembourg permanent establishment of a trade or business). For VAT purposes, however, the SCSp is itself a taxable person and must hold a VAT number in its own name for the customs-brokerage activity, notwithstanding its direct-tax transparency.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg has no check-the-box classification; the SCSp's fiscal transparency arises by operation of law. The following statutory options and elections interact with the SCSp and its owners: (1) Fiscal unity (Art. 164bis LIR) - available to Luxembourg-resident corporate taxpayers holding directly or indirectly at least 95% of a subsidiary for a qualifying holding period; it is unavailable to the transparent SCSp itself but usable by a corporate partner consolidating its own Luxembourg subsidiaries. (2) VAT elections - the small-enterprise franchise exemption below EUR 35,000 may be waived; the Union/Non-Union One-Stop-Shop (OSS) may be elected for distance sales of goods and certain B2C services; the reverse-charge mechanism governs the brokerage's cross-border B2B supplies. (3) Hybrid mismatch alignment - the ATAD 2 anti-hybrid provisions may recharacterise the transparency of the SCSp where a partner jurisdiction classifies it as fiscally opaque; the partnership agreement must allocate profits in a manner that avoids hybrid mismatches. (4) Customs authorisations - the broker may elect for AEO status (AEO-C/AEO-S), simplified declaration procedures and the 24-hour release channel; these are administrative authorisations, not tax elections. (5) Tax consolidation is not available to partnerships.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), operating within the Eurosystem of the European Central Bank (ECB); prudential and AML/CFT banking supervision is exercised by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) under the Law of 5 April 1993 and CSSF Regulation 12-02.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible on both current and capital account and Luxembourg satisfies IMF Article VIII obligations. There are no exchange controls on profit remittances, dividend distributions, or capital account repatriations; an SCSp engaged in customs brokerage may transfer operating profits and fee income to non-resident LPs without BCL authorization. The only compliance gate is the banking AML/KYC process, including source-of-funds verification for outward payments. As a euro-area member, Luxembourg applies no convertibility licensing or approval regime for trade-related payments.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Luxembourg has no statutory timeline, mandatory conversion ratio, or surrender requirement for export proceeds or customs brokerage receivables. The SCSp may freely retain earnings in EUR or any foreign currency and may convert at market rates. For any cross-border remittance exceeding EUR 12,500, the reporting bank files a BCL balance-of-payments statistical declaration; this is a data-reporting obligation, not a repatriation or surrender rule. If counterparties in third countries apply their own FX-rationing, the SCSp must contractually require settlement in euros or freely transferable currencies to remain fully compliant.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.international_payments_regulatory_compli: All EUR-denominated transfers within the EEA must be executed under SEPA rules with equal charges; no minimum or maximum value restrictions apply. Outbound USD/CHF/GBP payments must respect EU sanctions regimes and the EU Terrorist Financing Tracking Programme, and each MT103 must contain an accurate purpose code and the SCSp's registered name to avoid reference-data mismatches.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account (compte de blocage and compte courant)
Operational Account with customs duty SEPA Direct Debit mandate and FX treasury line
Operational Account and documentary trade finance facilities
Capital Escrow Account (subscription receipts from non-resident LPs)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low-Medium. A CSSF-licensed electronic money institution established in Luxembourg (e.g., Mangopay SA) can provide an EUR IBAN for fee collection and cross-border payouts, but cannot serve as the primary treasury rail because the Administration des douanes et accises requires a statutory bank-issued guarantee and a SEPA Direct Debit mandate under the deferred customs payment scheme (paiement différé), which EMIs are generally not structured to support. Passported EU EMIs under PSD2 are viable only as annex collection accounts with monthly volume below EUR 100,000 and cannot execute the documentary letter of credit (MT700) or standby guarantee (MT760) rails, nor provide the BCL balance-of-payments reporting on behalf of the SCSp.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For the five tier-1 banks selected above, at least one physical interview of the general partner (associé gérant) and all beneficial owners with a stake of 25% or more is required for a newly incorporated SCSp. Remote video onboarding with eIDAS-qualified signatures is permitted only for existing clients with an active relationship of at least 12 months. The physical interview must be supported by the statutory customs broker authorization, the EORI certificate, the RCS (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés) extract, and the notarized partnership deed. Delegated opening via power of attorney is acceptable only where the mandate is apostilled or legalized and the appointed representative has an existing Luxembourg banking footprint.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: SCSp tax-transparent classification: the bank may profile the partnership as a zero-tax hybrid or discretionary investment vehicle, triggering automatic high-risk treatment.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver: (i) Luxembourg Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (RBE) extract; (ii) CRS and FATCA self-certification confirming Passive NFE status; (iii) a partner-level Luxembourg tax opinion confirming pass-through taxation and attribution of customs brokerage income to each resident partner; (iv) evidence of operational substance, including issued brokerage invoices and VAT returns demonstrating active business revenue rather than passive financial income.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Zero minimum capital characteristic of the SCSp: the bank's credit committee may suspect a shell or letterbox entity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver: (i) notarized partnership agreement with a binding capital commitment schedule; (ii) 12-month cash-flow projection including customs duty bond utilization; (iii) executed Luxembourg office lease and employment contracts for the general manager and AML compliance officer; (iv) the customs broker license under Article 18 of Regulation (EU) 952/2013 and an EORI certificate for the SCSp.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money laundering red flag inherent to bonded transit management: cross-border third-country payments with suspended duties may indicate over/under-invoicing.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver: (i) AEO-C or AEO-F authorization (Authorised Economic Operator), or credible application evidence; (ii) complete NCTS transit movement records and import declarations for the two most recent quarters; (iii) a third-party audit engagement letter establishing accounting traceability; (iv) a signed undertaking that all client funds are segregated in a tier account (compte de tiers) with zero cash settlement; (v) a list of the ten highest-volume counterparties with EORI references and jurisdiction risk ratings.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: 100% non-resident ownership allowance of the SCSp: UBOs outside the EU will be scrutinized for shell risk and potential customs facilitation abuse.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver: (i) evidence of operational seat in Luxembourg with premises, telephone, IT infrastructure, and management presence; (ii) declaration by the general partner that all customs representation activity is executed exclusively from Luxembourg; (iii) bank-outflow evidence of payroll, social security (CNS) contributions, and Luxembourg VAT payments originated from the SCSp account; (iv) for non-EU LPs above 25%, an independent source-of-wealth report and negative-media screening from a recognized due-diligence provider.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: LP capital contributions are routed to the capital escrow account at BGL BNP Paribas or Banque de Luxembourg. EUR subscriptions settle by SEPA Credit Transfer with purpose code indicating equity injection into the SCSp; non-EUR subscriptions settle by SWIFT MT103 with the narrative including the SCSp RCS number and VAT matricule. The bank executes CSSF 12-02 due diligence, matches remitters to the RBE registry, and automatically files the BCL balance-of-payments statistical declaration for every cross-border remittance exceeding EUR 12,500. For non-EU LP transfers, the MT103 must identify the underlying LP entity, and funds originating from virtual-asset channels are not admissible. A blocked-account release condition is set for the notarial certificate evidencing the formation of the SCSp.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Customs duties and import VAT are collected by the Administration des douanes et accises through a SEPA Core Direct Debit mandate on the BIL operational account under the deferred payment scheme (paiement différé); this constitutes the Luxembourg automated broker interface, the counterpart of a customs ACH. Intra-EU trade settlements use instant SEPA or SWIFT MT103; non-EU counterparty disbursements use SWIFT MT103 and MT202 COV with accurate Union Customs Code narrative codes. High-value bonded freight purchases are settled by documentary letters of credit under UCP 600 (MT700/MT710), and the customs transit guarantee is provided by a standby Letter of Credit (MT760) or a comprehensive sûreté douanière pledged by the relationship bank. USD/CHF settlement amounts above EUR 50,000 are converted through the bank's standing FX instruction to preserve liquidity and netting discipline.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable FX forwards (EUR/USD, EUR/CHF, EUR/GBP) for customs brokerage receivables and duty settlement on a rolling 6-12 month maturity profile
Non-deliverable forwards (NDF) referencing the offshore offshore renminbi (CNH) and other restricted-liquidity currencies encountered in the Pan-European transit and bonded-warehouse corridor
FX swaps (tom-next and spot-next) for same-day liquidity management of the customs duty accumulation account
Cross-currency swap (EUR/USD) for the long-term equalization of USD-denominated subordinated loans from non-resident LPs
Vanilla FX options (call/put) for hedging tariff quotation exposure in volatile emerging-market currency pairs when the SCSp issues firm brokerage quotes

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts of the SCSp (comptes annuels) prepared, approved by the partners and filed electronically via eCDF/myRCSL
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCSL — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month following approval by the partners; approval must occur within six months of the financial year-end (standard 31 December year-end: filing no later than 31 July).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: RCSL formal demand and court order with fine of EUR 250–5,000 plus coercive daily fine (astreinte) of up to EUR 250 per day of delay; after two consecutive years of non-filing the Public Prosecutor may seek judicial dissolution (functional equivalent of administrative strike-off); the general partner (associé commandité) remains personally liable for continued operations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial ownership data (confirmation annuelle des bénéficiaires effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE — Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually, within one month following the anniversary of the SCSp's initial RBE registration date; any transfer of partnership interests must additionally be declared within one month of the change.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine of EUR 125–1,250 per violation; wilful concealment may trigger criminal penalties and management prohibitions; RBE may flag the entity as non-compliant and impose repeated fines until the annual confirmation is filed.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual maintenance and compliance confirmation of the customs brokerage authorization and customs-representation guarantee
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Customs and Excise Administration (Administration des douanes et accises — ADdA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Continuous obligation under EU UCC Article 39; updated supporting evidence must be supplied on ADdA request, at licence anniversary reviews, or upon any material change in establishment, management, partners, or AML compliance.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Suspension or revocation of the customs brokerage authorization; loss of customs-representation rights prevents lawful clearance and may trigger daily penalty assessments, forced cessation of customs activities, and revocation of any AEO or guarantee status.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent statutory audit is mandatory if the SCSp exceeds two of the three Luxembourg small-company thresholds at the balance-sheet date (total balance sheet above EUR 4.4 million; net turnover above EUR 8.8 million; average headcount above 50), or if the SCSp is a CSSF-regulated fund or AIFM vehicle; the audit must be performed by an approved statutory auditor (réviseur d'entreprises agréé).
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under the amended Law of 19 December 2002 (transposing EU Accounting Directive 2013/34/EU); IFRS as adopted by the EU is permitted for the individual accounts; electronic filing uses the eCDF XBRL taxonomy.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The general partner of the SCSp must file every transfer of partnership interests or change in beneficial ownership with the RBE within one month and must confirm the accuracy of the UBO file annually within one month of the registration anniversary; non-resident partners are identified to country-of-residence level; the SCSp's lack of separate legal personality creates no exemption, and the general partner is the statutory filer.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 2,500 – USD 6,000 per year (typical Luxembourg domiciliation/registered-office and corporate-agent market range; higher for regulated customs brokerage supporting AML files)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000 – USD 8,000 per year (typical certified statutory audit fee for a small-to-medium Luxembourg SCSp; lower if the partnership is below the audit threshold and only a limited review is commissioned)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: SCSp is fiscally transparent at Luxembourg level; the statutory corporate income tax benchmark of 24.94% therefore applies at the partner level, not at the SCSp entity level. Available preferential measures include the 80% exemption for qualifying IP income, the research and development super-deduction of up to 50% of eligible R&D expenditure, and the participation exemption for qualifying dividend and capital gain income. There is no general statutory tax holiday in Luxembourg.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulaire 510 - Annual corporate income tax and net wealth tax declaration; filed electronically through the Luxembourg direct tax e-filing portal (eCDF) / MyGuichet.lu. VAT and customs declarations are filed separately through eTVA and customs systems.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: No later than 31 December of the calendar year following the fiscal year-end; electronically filed returns are generally expected no later than 30 September of that year unless the ACD grants an extension.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal identification: registered name, RCS number, LEI, registered office, legal form and date of incorporation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the SCSp's full Luxembourg legal identity. Non-resident partners are identified in the partner allocation schedule, not as principal filers.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Place of effective management and Luxembourg tax residence status.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the central management of the SCSp is in Luxembourg, indicate Luxembourg residency. If management is abroad, attach the factual substance schedule and DTA position.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Balance sheet and statutory financial statements attachment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: File the complete audited or certified annual accounts of the SCSp; non-resident partners are not separately required to file Luxembourg accounts solely by reason of the SCSp allocation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income computation at SCSp level.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: SCSp taxable income is computed generally; the resulting profit or loss is then allocated to partners in accordance with the partnership agreement.
Non-resident partner expenses are not deductible in the SCSp return unless borne by the SCSp or attributable to a Luxembourg permanent establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax loss carryforward utilised in the current year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only Luxembourg-recognised losses properly allocated to the SCSp may be offset. A non-resident partner may not use losses outside the transparency allocation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: SCSp pass-through allocation and partner register schedule.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: List each partner's percentage, capital contribution, profit share, status (corporate or individual, resident or non-resident) and any change during the fiscal year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Signature of the authorised manager / legal representative and declaration of completeness.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident managing partner must appoint a Luxembourg tax resident authorised representative before filing if requested by the ACD.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing exposes the SCSp to administrative default assessment, procedural fines, and monthly late-payment interest at 0.6% per month. Willful omission or false declaration may attract criminal fines up to EUR 250,000, tax fraud penalties, and loss of the customs broker licence through revocation proceedings.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% statutory dividend withholding tax for Luxembourg corporate issuers. An SCSp is fiscally transparent, so profit allocations to partners are not treated as Luxembourg dividends at entity level and no 15% withholding tax applies to such allocations. A Luxembourg corporate partner may qualify for the 0% participation exemption / EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive rate on distributions made by a corporate underlying entity.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a Luxembourg income tax treaty, the beneficial owner must submit a valid tax residence certificate from its state of residence, accompanied by the required ACD relief/refund application, evidence of beneficial ownership, and substantiation of the underlying economic substance. Reduced-rate or exemption relief is applied before payment only where the application is accepted by the ACD; otherwise a refund claim is pursued through the Luxembourg statutory recovery procedure.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Luxembourg domestic law imposes no withholding tax on arm's length royalties or interest paid to non-residents. Treaty rates are generally 0% for both categories where treaty entitlement is established. Excessive royalties or interest paid to related partners may be recharacterised as constructive distributions, potentially exposing them to Luxembourg withholding tax at 15%.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 0 - no statutory de minimis threshold below which transfer pricing documentation is waived for the SCSp; the ACD may demand Master File, Local File and benchmarking documentation on request. Country-by-country reporting applies at the group level where consolidated turnover reaches EUR 750,000,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: No UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations exist in Luxembourg, but the Luxembourg anti-abuse doctrine, LIR anti-abuse provisions, and ATAD principles require genuine economic substance. A customs brokerage SCSp must maintain real managerial presence, employees, business premises, bank accounts, and risk-taking functions in Luxembourg; otherwise the ACD may disregard the SCSp, deny treaty benefits or the tax residence certificate, and impose joint liability on the managing partner.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate understatement of customs brokerage fees, omitted invoicing, fictitious deductible expenses, or making false statements in the annual tax filing with intent to evade Luxembourg income tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal tax fraud penalties, administrative default reassessment, monthly late interest of 0.6%, monetary fines up to EUR 250,000, and confiscation of the illegal economic advantage.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The managing partner and any board-equivalent persons may be personally prosecuted; aggravated tax fraud can result in imprisonment, travel bans, confiscation orders and civil restitution of the unpaid taxes.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the SCSp as a mere conduit with no Luxembourg office, staff, bank account, or effective decision-making, while using Luxembourg treaty benefits or the SCSp structure to shift profits from customs brokerage activities to non-resident related parties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of tax residence certificate, refusal of treaty benefits, recharacterisation of the structure under the Luxembourg anti-abuse doctrine, reassessment of diverted profits, and administrative penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and managers may be jointly liable for the tax liability where the corporate veil is pierced; criminal proceedings may also impose civil restitution, travel bans and imprisonment in cases of fraudulent use of the structure.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting client funds without proper KYC/AML vetting, processing payments through unmonitored omnibus accounts, failing to report suspicious transactions, or acting as a shell intermediary for unknown beneficial owners of imported or bonded goods.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Regulatory fines up to 10% of annual turnover under Luxembourg AML legislation, temporary or permanent revocation of the customs broker licence, and confiscation of proceeds of money laundering.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: AML responsible officers and directors face personal criminal liability, including imprisonment, travel bans, director disqualification, and orders for civil restitution of laundered amounts.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer pricing mispricing and concealed quasi-distributions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging non-arm's-length brokerage commissions or management fees to related foreign logistics parties, stripping Luxembourg taxable profit, or making payments to non-resident partners without economic substance and without transfer pricing documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Transfer pricing adjustment, additional corporate income tax, monthly interest, administrative penalties, and recharacterisation of excessive payments as constructive distributions subject to Luxembourg withholding tax at 15%.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and managing partners may be held personally liable for withheld taxes and civil damages; deliberate or grossly negligent conduct can lead to criminal sanctions, travel bans and imprisonment.
